steps.title: The fleet and its year at sea
steps.say: An invented operator with six container ships on the North Atlantic, after a year of passages between New York, Norfolk, Halifax and Rotterdam, Antwerp, Le Havre and Hamburg: every voyage's noon reports and AIS positions. A fuel model is fitted for each ship on its first ten months of noon reports and scored on the last two against the yard's sea-trial curve; the fouling term says how much more fuel the hull now costs than when it was clean. Two noon reports arrive through the gateway: one accepted and scored, one refused with the reason.

steps.title: Plan the crossing: the route
steps.say: Atlantic Sage is to sail from New York to Rotterdam, 90% loaded, on a charter that wants her at Rotterdam inside a 36-hour berth window, with hire of $28,000 a day, fuel at $620 a tonne, carbon at $80 a tonne on half her CO2 (the EU ETS share) and $3,000 an hour if she is late. The route optimiser searches the ocean grid with the forecast issued at departure, at the speed that lands mid-window, against the shortest sea route at the same speed.

steps.title: Speed, the ETA band and bunkers
steps.say: Along the route, the speed optimiser chooses an order for every leg of about 120 miles, weighing fuel and carbon against hire, waiting at anchor and the late penalty. The plan is sailed through 24 forecast members to get its ETA band, and it keeps its P90 inside the window. Inside the charter terms, so it is activated without an approval. The bunker planner then decides where to buy for this voyage and the next two legs.

steps.title: Two days out: a storm and a full Rotterdam
steps.say: The generator is told that a storm will form 60 hours after departure and cross her planned track around day four, and that Rotterdam cannot berth her before 17 October 06:00, 30 hours after her window closes. The departure forecast could not know either. She sails two days; the monitor then reads a fresh forecast and Rotterdam's line-up and raises what it finds. Plan against actual so far, split into speed, weather and the model.

steps.title: Compare the alternatives
steps.say: From where she is, with the new forecast and Rotterdam's line-up: keep the plan, hold the ETA already given to the charterer, re-speed on the same route, or re-route and re-speed. Each is sailed through the 24 members: ETA band, fuel, CO2, the charter penalty, waiting at anchor and the worst sea on the way.

steps.title: Change the plan, with a second person
steps.say: The operator puts the re-routed, re-speeded plan forward. It moves the ETA far beyond the 12 hours the charter allows without notice, so it becomes a proposal: the operator cannot approve their own, and the master does. The charterer's ETA is updated and the ship sails the new plan.

steps.title: Arrival and the voyage report
steps.say: She sails on to Rotterdam. At berthing the voyage report compares what she burned and paid with the weather-normalised baseline: the same departure on the shortest sea route at service speed, through the same weather, storm included, then waiting for the berth. Then plan against actual for the whole voyage, and the audit trail.
